experiment: NLU-07 — Read -> said -> read: does meaning survive a round trip?
notes: `_triple_sentence` is the ONE place a held fact becomes words, so this measures understanding against expression: what the substrate SAYS of a claim must read back as the same claim
cannot judge the article in “a robin is a bird” — the store holds no word class for the complement
cannot judge the article in “a vault is a locked” — the store holds no word class for the complement
cannot judge the article in “a dog is an animal” — the store holds no word class for the complement
cannot judge the article in “a robin is a mammal” — the store holds no word class for the complement
said back: 'A robin is a bird.' -> “a robin is a bird”
said back: 'The vault is locked.' -> “a vault is a locked”
said back: 'A dog is an animal.' -> “a dog is an animal”
said back: 'A robin is not a mammal.' -> “a robin is a mammal”

checks.name: round trip: 'A robin is a bird.'
checks.detail: said “a robin is a bird” -> ('robin_bird',) [derived:subject_relation_object_polarity], wanted ('robin_bird',)

checks.name: round trip: 'The vault is locked.'
checks.detail: said “a vault is a locked” -> ('vault_locked',) [derived:subject_relation_object_polarity], wanted ('vault_locked',)

checks.name: can say back: 'The control rod is heavy.'
checks.detail: the chain read it as ('control_rod_heavy',) but no clause parts exist to render, so it cannot state what it understood
